items.title: NetInjectBench: Benchmarking Indirect Prompt Injection in Tool-Using Large Language Model Agents for Network Operations
items.raw_content:
Authors: Ruksat Khan Shayoni, Muhammad Faraz Shoaib, S M Asif Hossain, M. F. Mridha

Tool-using large language model (LLM) agents are attractive for network operations, but tickets, alerts, logs, runbooks, and ChatOps messages can carry indirect prompt injections. We present NetInjectBench, a 130-scenario benchmark that separates untrusted artifact text, trusted policy metadata, and evaluation labels for network-operation tool use. The sample contains 40 benign, 40 weak-attack, 40 strong-attack, and 10 approved high-impact change scenarios; each is evaluated with Qwen2.5-7B, Llama3.1-8B, and Mistral-7B. Across 240 attack instances, naive execution reached an 82.50% unsafe tool-action rate. Prompt-only safety, Self-Reminder, Spotlighting, and a Two-Pass LLM Judge reduced this rate to 25.63%, 21.67%, 18.33%, and 10.00%, respectively. Static allowlisting reached 5.00% but blocked all approved changes, yielding 0.00% usefulness and 100.00% overblocking on approved cases. Under the stated metadata-integrity assumption, the metadata-aware policy gate produced 0/240 unsafe attack actions, with a 95% Wilson upper bound of 1.58%, while preserving 99.17% attack-scenario usefulness and 100.00% approved-change usefulness. The findings show that network-operation agents need execution-time authorization boundaries alongside prompt-level instruction hygiene.
items.title_zh: NetInjectBench：面向网络运维工具型 LLM Agent 的间接提示注入基准
items.summary: NetInjectBench is a 130-scenario benchmark for indirect prompt injection in tool-using LLM agents for network operations. Across 240 attack instances naive execution produced an 82.50% unsafe tool-action rate, while a metadata-aware policy gate produced no unsafe actions under a stated metadata-integrity assumption.

items.title: Scalable Optimal Transport Algorithm for Network Alignment
items.raw_content:
Authors: Elaheh Hassani, Durga Mandarapu, Qi Yu, Hanghang Tong, Ariful Azad

Network alignment identifies node correspondences across different networks and is a fundamental primitive in many data science applications, including social network analysis, fraud detection, and knowledge graph integration. However, state-of-the-art network alignment methods often achieve high accuracy by repeatedly constructing and updating dense matrices, sacrificing scalability in the process. To address this scalability limitation without compromising alignment accuracy, we present FastAlign, a scalable, sparsity-aware framework for optimal transport-based network alignment. Rather than introducing a new alignment model, FastAlign preserves the original OT formulation and reinterprets its computation as a set of recurring mixed sparse-dense operations. FastAlign combines sparsity-aware graph computation with domain-specific kernel fusion, including a custom SpMM kernel. Our results show that FastAlign achieves alignment quality comparable to state-of-the-art OT-based methods while substantially reducing end-to-end runtime up to 3.89x-9.45x on CPU and 2.24x-32.54x on GPU.
items.title_zh: 面向网络对齐的可扩展最优传输算法
items.summary: FastAlign is a sparsity-aware framework for optimal transport-based network alignment that keeps the original OT formulation and recasts it as recurring mixed sparse-dense operations with kernel fusion, including a custom SpMM kernel. It matches state-of-the-art alignment quality while cutting end-to-end runtime by up to 3.89x-9.45x on CPU and 2.24x-32.54x on GPU.

items.title: AI 2040 and the cult of intelligence
items.raw_content: I used to be one of these people. I read Yudkowsky and was like, OMG recursive self improvement hard takeoff AI is coming. Then I joined the real world and actually tried to do things. At comma, we ship a hardware product of similar complexity to a cell phone, and it’s really hard. Reality has lots of finicky details. I would like to see the authors of this document try to change a bike tire. Even with a superintelligent ChatGPT, I suspect they would struggle.
items.title_zh: AI 2040 与智能崇拜
items.summary: A blog post pushes back on recursive self-improvement and hard-takeoff predictions, arguing from the author's experience at comma that shipping complex hardware is hard and full of finicky details. The author suspects even a superintelligent ChatGPT would struggle to change a bike tire.

items.title: Stop Telling Me to Ask an LLM
items.raw_content: I'm a million times more likely to send an email or a text than to pick up the phone. But I had a question I thought was worth an actual call, so I scheduled one with someone senior enough to have real scar tissue, the kind you only get from watching a decision go sideways in a boardroom. I asked him where he'd look, personally, for the answer to a hard question I was chasing, one without industry consensus. If five studies conflicted, which would he trust? I wanted the thing 30 years had taught him that a search engine couldn't. That stung a little, but it wasn't the first time I'd heard it. Once it was a data problem I'd been stuck on. I'd approached it a half dozen different ways and could explain in some detail why none of them had worked. I reached out to a few people who do this kind of thing for a living, people I text with regularly, trading questions and working through whatever
items.title_zh: 别再叫我什么都去问 LLM
items.summary: An essay recounts seeking a seasoned operator's judgment on a hard, contested question and argues that the kind of experience a search engine cannot supply is not something an LLM can replace either.

items.title: How the FSF sysadmins block botnets with reaction
items.raw_content: I have written about the FSF facing DDoS attacks several times, including on doing our part to clean up the internet and on Uptime Kuma , as well as "Defending Savannah from DDoS attacks" . But I realized recently that I left out an important tool that we use extensively. Today I will talk about reaction . With the rise of aggressive scrapers building datasets to train LLMs, we needed to invest a lot of resources into thwarting the attackers. During this journey, we had several growing pains. We noticed patterns in the scrapers that were abnormal, which gave us material for writing regular expressions. Searching for the regular expression then gave us a large lists of IP addresses. Looking up the origin of those IP addresses revealed that some of the crawlers were using botnets of residential IP addresses to scrape faster and avoid detection.
items.title_zh: FSF 系统管理员如何用 reaction 封堵僵尸网络
items.summary: FSF sysadmins describe using a tool called reaction to turn abnormal scraper patterns into regular expressions, which surfaced large lists of IP addresses. Some of the crawlers were found to be using botnets of residential IPs to scrape faster and avoid detection, a problem that grew as aggressive scrapers built datasets to train LLMs.

items.title: The kids with phones are alright
items.raw_content: T here was a remarkable video going around the Scottish socials yesterday which led to quite a bit of media coverage . It’s a four-minute long video showing some furious Scotrail passengers confronting a drunk middle-aged pervert who is quietly filming a group of quiet, sober 16- and 17-year old girls heading home from a night out. It really is worth a watch, because it’s a four-minute long documentary masterclass in bystander action, documenting offenses, holding perpetrators to account, centering the victims, and somehow staying calm and focused even when you want to batter the fuck out of someone who has it coming.
items.title_zh: 用手机的孩子们没什么问题
items.summary: The post highlights a four-minute video in which ScotRail passengers confront a drunk man who was filming a group of sober 16- and 17-year-old girls, praising it as a masterclass in calm bystander action.

items.title: Nvidia, CoreWeave, and Nebius: Inside the Circular Financing of the GPU Boom
items.raw_content: Neoclouds are one of the more hotly debated AI business models, with CoreWeave and Nebius being the two most widely recognized names. These companies have seen their sales, backlog, and share prices soar. Yet, supporting their growth is extremely expensive, and neoclouds do not have the same cash nor operating cash flow profiles of Big Tech. This is leading neoclouds to employ unique and circular financing structures, raising some red flags.
items.title_zh: Nvidia、CoreWeave 与 Nebius：GPU 热潮中的循环融资
items.summary: An analysis examines the circular financing structures neoclouds such as CoreWeave and Nebius use to fund expensive growth, warning that their cash and operating cash flow profiles differ sharply from Big Tech's.

items.title: NanoVSR: Towards Real-Time Video Super-Resolution on Edge Devices
items.title_zh: NanoVSR：面向边缘设备的实时视频超分辨率
items.summary: NanoVSR is a fully convolutional video super-resolution architecture that uses structural reparameterization to collapse into standard convolutions at inference, avoiding transformers, explicit optical flow and custom operators while learning spatio-temporal alignment implicitly through progressive training. On REDS4, the 644k-parameter variant reports 28.64 dB PSNR at 27.2 FPS on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX 16GB at 25W, and a 1.7M variant reaches 29.15 dB at 19.58 FPS.

items.title: Hallucination Detection in Large Language Models Using Diversion Decoding
items.title_zh: 使用转向解码检测大语言模型幻觉
items.summary: The paper proposes diversion decoding, which actively challenges model-generated responses during decoding and extracts features capturing the model's resistance to producing alternative answers, then trains a machine-learning model on these features as an uncertainty heuristic for hallucination detection. The authors report it outperforms existing methods with significantly lower computational complexity.

items.title: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Physics: Post-training LLMs with Continuous Rewards
items.title_zh: 以可验证物理为依据的强化学习：用连续奖励后训练 LLM
items.summary: RLVP is an RL post-training framework for multi-PDE solver code generation that pairs hard program-validity checks with continuous physics rewards scoring function-space accuracy and PDE-residual consistency. A single policy post-trained across hyperbolic, parabolic, elliptic and incompressible-flow PDE families is reported to improve over pretrained and supervised-only baselines, transfer zero-shot to held-out PDEs, and recombine numerical motifs such as stencils, time-stepping schemes and boundary-handling primitives.

items.title: When Reasoning Hurts Legal Drafting: The Verbalization Bottleneck in Patent Claim Generation
items.title_zh: 当推理损害法律起草：专利权利要求生成中的言语化瓶颈
items.summary: The paper proposes a task-specific chain-of-thought method for patent claim generation and evaluates it with automatic metrics and human expert assessment, finding that reasoning-enhanced prompting can improve claim quality but that implicit CoT, which keeps reasoning internal, consistently outperforms explicit CoT. It attributes this gap to abstraction of critical details, disruption of internalized generation patterns, and cascading error propagation.

items.title: ARMOR: Stabilizing On-Policy LLM RL with Off-Policy Anchor Samples
items.title_zh: ARMOR：用离策略锚点样本稳定在策略 LLM 强化学习
items.summary: ARMOR targets over-optimization instability in on-policy LLM reinforcement learning, arguing that reverse KL regularization is often insufficient for covering the reference distribution, and adds Anchor Rollout that reuses off-policy data from the reference policy plus a Mixed Optimization objective that enables controlled exploration without auxiliary losses. Experiments on reasoning benchmarks are reported to mitigate validation collapse and sustain performance improvements over extended training.

items.title: Temporary Authority, Permanent Effects: Commit-Time Authorization for LLM Agents
items.title_zh: 临时授权，永久影响：LLM 智能体的提交时授权
items.summary: The paper defines commit-time authorization, requiring that the evidence authorizing a durable effect remain fresh, causally prior, bound to the same effect and eligible at commit time, and builds a controlled-invalidation suite spanning browser, tool and API, and multi-agent workflows. In the primary 54-task matrix only 55 of 270 runs are authorized completions, and the authors evaluate a fail-closed boundary monitor, CommitGuard, as a mitigation.
